olympiad_full_name: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad
statement: Find all $n\geq 3$ for which $n$ distinct reals can be arranged on a circle so each equals the product of its two neighbors.
source: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad 2015

source: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad 2015

olympiad_full_name: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad
statement: Cyclic quadrilateral $ABCD$ with $AB<CD$; $P=AD\cap BC$. Circumcircle of $\triangle PCD$ meets line $AB$ at $Q,R$; tangents from $P$ to circumcircle of $ABCD$ touch at $S,T$. (a) Prove $PQ=PR$. (b) Prove $QRST$ is cyclic.
source: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad 2015

olympiad_full_name: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad
statement: Anselmo and Bonifacio alternate: each turn, replace the board number by its number of divisors or by the number minus its number of divisors. First to write 0 wins. Initial number: 1036. Who wins?
source: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad 2015

olympiad_full_name: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad
statement: $\triangle ABC$ with $AC=2AB$; $D=$ angle bisector from $A$ meets $BC$; $F=$ intersection of the line through $C$ parallel to $AB$ with the perpendicular to $AD$ through $A$. Prove $FD$ passes through the midpoint of $AC$.
source: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad 2015

olympiad_full_name: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad
statement: 39 students, 6 problems (0 or 1 point each). For any 3 students, at most 1 problem was unsolved by all three. Let $B$ = sum of all scores. Find the minimum possible $B$.
source: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad 2015
